chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Rifāʿah al-Nakhkhās, from a man, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام offered condolences to a man over his son and said to him: “Allah is better for your son than you are, and the reward of Allah is better for you than he was.”
Then when news reached him of the man’s intense grief after that, he returned to him and said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله has died; do you not have in him an example?”

He said, “He was murhaqan.” So he said: “Indeed, before him are three qualities: the testimony that there is no god but Allah, the mercy of Allah, and the intercession of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله; not one of them will miss him, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.”

key_terms.أُسْوَةٌ: an example to be followed and taken as consolation
key_terms.جَزَعِهِ: his intense grief and impatience at affliction
key_terms.رَحْمَةَ اللَّهِ: Allah’s mercy extended to the deceased
key_terms.شَفَاعَةَ: intercession on behalf of the believer
key_terms.شَهَادَةَ: the testimony of faith affirming divine unity
key_terms.عَزَّى: offered condolences and comforted the bereaved
key_terms.مُرَهَّقًا: a youth affected by burden or moral strain

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام console a parent after the death of a child?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches patience and restraint in grief at the loss of a child, reminding the bereaved that Allah’s care for the deceased and Allah’s reward for the parent are greater. It also offers hope for the deceased through shahadah, divine mercy, and the intercession of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
